question: Is the width-dependent QI-removal behavior exposed by C4E/C4F robust to a secondary depth-weighted mass-neutral theta norm, or is it primarily a consequence of the historically frozen equal-coordinate shape metric?

C2_metric.historical_primary: unweighted RMS over mass-neutral mean-theta shape components

metric_policy.role: interpretation sensitivity only; cannot retroactively change C2/C3/C4E decisions

preregistered_outputs: unweighted and depth-weighted pooled local shape RMS
unweighted and depth-weighted pooled non-QI remainder RMS
fraction of intervals improved/worsened in both metrics
depth-weighted QI dot remainder and cosine
fraction of intervals whose QI-removal direction changes between metrics
squared-norm identity residual in both metrics
C4F QI-counterfactual admissibility count retained as interpretation boundary

decision_logic.WIDTH_EFFECT_ROBUST_TO_DEPTH_WEIGHTING: For WT_RISE in both dt routes, QI removal worsens the pooled shape norm at 2.5 cm and improves it at 5 cm under both historical and depth-weighted metrics. No fitted tolerance is used; the boundary is ratio=1.
decision_logic.WIDTH_EFFECT_METRIC_SENSITIVE: The WT_RISE 2.5-versus-5 cm pooled removal direction is not preserved under the depth-weighted metric in both routes.
decision_logic.C4G_DIAGNOSTIC_BLOCKED: Required identities, predecessor authority or route completion fails.

claim_boundary: Secondary weighting does not replace the historical primary metric.
No groundwater feedback, application acceptance, performance or production claim is authorized.
